en.title: Smallest Digit String After Incrementing and Reinserting
en.description:
One operation takes out any digit d, changes it to min(d+1,9), and inserts it at any position. You may perform any number of operations (including 0). Find the lexicographically smallest final string, keeping leading zeros.

Standard input/output, examples and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's do not claim to be the source's original limits.
en.input: One line containing a digit string of length 1..200000.
en.output: Output the lexicographically smallest digit string, keeping leading zeros.
en.explanation: Example 1: 6 and 5 have a smaller 4 to their right, so they are moved and become 7 and 6; sorting them together with the kept 2, 4 and 7 gives 24677. Example 2: doing nothing is already the smallest, so the output is 0. Example 3: take 2 out, turning it into 3, and insert it after 1 to get 13.
hints: Go from right to left, maintaining the minimum digit to the right. If the current digit is larger than that minimum, it must be moved and incremented; all others are kept. Finally, sort the transformed digits.
